props.name: reveal
props.description: `hover`: with a mouse, the actions stay hidden until the row is hovered, holds focus, is `active` or has a menu open. Give the button `variant="ghost"` here. On a touch screen (`pointer: coarse`) they show at rest. In a compact row without `InboxItemTrailing`, put them last in `InboxItemContent`: they centre on the row and both lines end short of them, the time and the marks moving over and staying visible (room for one 32px button). In `InboxItemTrailing` they take the place of the timestamp, the marks and the attention dot, which step aside; on a touch screen the rest of the trailing column moves over to make room.

props.name: reveal
props.description: `hover`, for an older row in a compact list: hidden at rest, so the title takes its room. It shows in the same place, without animation, while the row is hovered or it or a control in it holds keyboard focus; a touch screen never hovers, so there it stays hidden. While hidden it isn't read out: say the time in the trigger's name.

name: InboxItemLeadingBadge
description: A small badge in the bottom-right corner of `InboxItemLeading`, the corner a presence light takes, holding one icon: on a thread or task row in a channel, the channel's own icon on the thread's or task's `IconTile`; in a direct message, the thread's or task's mark on the other side's `Avatar`. Put it inside `InboxItemLeading`, after the tile or avatar, with one icon as its child; leave the avatar's `AvatarBadge` out, since the corner holds one mark. It is hidden from assistive technology unless given a `role`.

name: InboxItemSkeleton
description: A placeholder for one `InboxItem` while the list loads. It is an `InboxItem` itself, with the same parts as the loaded row (an optional leading block, the context line, the title, the excerpt, the timestamp), each holding a bar instead of text; a compact one has no trailing column, its time at the end of the heading. The padding, the divider and every line's height are the loaded row's, so nothing moves when the content arrives. Match `density`, `leading` and `context` to the rows it stands for. Hidden from assistive technology: mark the region that stays while the list loads `aria-busy`.

props.name: context
props.description: A context line above the title, where the rows have an `InboxItemContext`.

props.name: density
props.description: The density of the rows it stands for.

props.name: leading
props.description: A 35px block where the rows have an `InboxItemLeading` avatar or tile.

props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component.

name: InboxItemSkeletonList
description: The list of `InboxItemSkeleton` rows that stands in for a list of `InboxItem` rows while it loads, with nothing between or around the rows that the loaded list doesn't have (no border, no card): only the list's 2px gap, which the loaded list has too (design/patterns/lists.md). Renders `count` rows of the given shape, or its children, once `delay` (1 second by default) has passed. It isn't `aria-busy` itself: it goes away when the content arrives, so mark the region that stays, such as the list's panel or viewport, `aria-busy` while it loads.

props.name: context
props.description: A context line above the title, where the rows have an `InboxItemContext`.

props.name: count
props.description: How many rows to show. About a screenful; ignored when there are children.

props.name: delay
props.description: Milliseconds to wait before the rows appear, so a fast load doesn't flash them (Feedback, "Empty, loading and failed"). The list is empty until then. A list skeleton is only for a slow load, so it waits 1 second by default; pass `0` to show the rows at once.

props.name: density
props.description: The density of the rows it stands for.

props.description: A 35px block where the rows have an `InboxItemLeading` avatar or tile.
